          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci patch-coverage

name: putitoutthere pypi tag

# Cuts the git tag for each PyPI package the release run delegated, AFTER
# the caller's `pypi-publish` job has uploaded it. Issue #623.
#
# Why this is a separate job in the consumer's workflow rather than a step
# inside the reusable `release.yml`:
#
#   PyPI's upload cannot run inside a cross-repo reusable workflow —
#   Trusted Publisher matching filters candidates by repository_owner /
#   repository_name before checking job_workflow_ref, so a token minted in
#   here never matches the consumer's TP record (pypi/warehouse#11096; see
#   notes/audits/2026-04-28-pypi-tp-reusable-workflow-constraint.md). The
#   upload therefore lives in the caller's own `pypi-publish` job.
#
#   A git tag is the record of what shipped. Cutting it in the release job
#   — before the caller's job has run, or when a failure on an unrelated
#   registry means it never will — put tags on consumers' remotes naming
#   versions that were never uploaded, recoverable only by deleting the
#   tag by hand (#623). So the tag follows the upload.
#
# Consumers compose with this workflow, not with the CLI-wrapping action
# (design-commitments non-goal #10): all the wiring — checkout, committer
# identity, the engine invocation — lives here, where it is versioned with
# the engine that it runs.
#
# The tag follows REGISTRY truth, not a step's exit code: `reconcile` reads
# each package's live version and writes the tag only for a version that is
# actually on the registry and has none. That makes it idempotent (a
# re-run is a no-op), self-healing (it also backfills any tag an earlier
# run failed to push), and incapable of recording an upload that silently
# uploaded nothing.
#
# Consumer usage (their own .github/workflows/release.yml) — see
# README → "Publishing to PyPI":
#
#   pypi-tag:
#     needs: pypi-publish
#     uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/pypi-tag.yml@v0
#     permissions:
#       contents: write

on:
  workflow_call:

jobs:
  tag:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      # Full history + tags: the engine compares each package's live
      # registry version against the tags that already exist, and a
      # shallow clone carries none of them.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Configure git identity for tagging
        # Annotated tags require committer identity; hosted runners have
        # none by default.
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      # No setup-node: the action is a `node24` action (GitHub supplies
      # the runtime) and `reconcile` reads every registry over `fetch` —
      # no `npm` / `cargo` / `twine` subprocess to provision.
      - name: Tag every published version that has no tag
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        with:
          command: reconcile

name: Release (dogfood)

# putitoutthere releases itself using itself.
#
# On push to main OR manual dispatch:
#   1. `putitoutthere plan` against the committed putitoutthere.toml
#      + the current HEAD trailer, emit matrix JSON to GITHUB_OUTPUT.
#   2. If the plan is non-empty, the publish job rebuilds the ncc
#      action bundle, folds it into a release-only commit (the bundle
#      is gitignored on main and lives only on tag commits), then
#      `putitoutthere publish` does the npm publish, writeVersion,
#      and tagging — tag points at the bundle-bearing commit.
#   3. The floating `v<major>` tag is moved to the new release commit
#      so scaffolded consumer workflows (`uses: ...@v1`) resolve to a
#      ref that has `dist-action/index.js` under it.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: release
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write
  id-token: write

jobs:
  plan:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.matrix }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build SDK
        run: pnpm run build

      - id: plan
        name: putitoutthere plan
        run: pnpm exec putitoutthere plan --json > plan.json
      - name: expose matrix
        run: |
          # #412: plan --json is now { matrix, verdicts, skew }; the matrix
          # output stays the bare array the publish gate + build consume.
          # shellcheck disable=SC2002
          printf 'matrix=%s\n' "$(cat plan.json | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(JSON.parse(d).matrix)))")" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Plan:"
          # shellcheck disable=SC2002
          cat plan.json | node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{const m=JSON.parse(d).matrix;console.log(m.length? m.map(r=>' - '+r.name+'@'+r.version+' ('+r.target+')').join('\n') : '(nothing to release)');})"

  publish:
    needs: plan
    if: fromJSON(needs.plan.outputs.matrix || '[]')[0] != null
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: npm
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node
        with:
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Build SDK
        run: pnpm run build

      - name: Rebuild action bundle
        run: pnpm run build:action

      - name: Configure git
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      # `dist-action/` is gitignored on main; the action bundle exists only on
      # tag commits. Fold the freshly-built bundle into a release-only commit
      # so the per-package tag (and the floating `v<major>` tag that tracks
      # it) resolve to a commit that contains `dist-action/index.js`. The
      # commit is not pushed to main — it lives only as the tag's target.
      #
      # The stage / empty-index guard / trailer-forwarding commit — and the
      # reason the parent body must survive (else the publish-time plan
      # re-derivation silently downgrades `release: minor` to a patch; the
      # 0.1.51 → 0.2.0 attempt that landed as 0.1.52) — now live in the
      # `fold-bundle` engine command as tested code (`src/fold-action-bundle.ts`),
      # not inline bash. See notes/handoff/2026-04-24-dist-action.md.
      - name: Fold action bundle into release commit
        run: |
          pnpm exec putitoutthere fold-bundle --subject 'chore(release): bundle action'

      - name: putitoutthere publish
        env:
          # The repository-visibility preflight check calls the GitHub
          # API; an authenticated call gets 5000 req/hr instead of the
          # unauthenticated 60, so a busy runner never rate-limits.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          # npm's trusted-publishing (OIDC) exchange never throws: every
          # failure path in npm's `lib/utils/oidc.js` is
          # `log.verbose(...); return undefined`. When the exchange fails,
          # setup-node's placeholder `_authToken`
          # (`XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX`) survives in `.npmrc`, the PUT goes
          # out with a bogus bearer, and npm masks the rejection as a bare
          # `E404 Not Found - PUT`. Nothing at the default loglevel says
          # why — see run 30456638828, where 0.2.80 failed exactly this
          # way with no diagnosable cause in the log.
          #
          # `verbose` surfaces the one line that names it:
          #   npm verbose oidc Failed token exchange request with body
          #   message: <reason>
          #
          # Safe to leave on: npm logs the id-token *request* URL (the
          # bearer is a header, not a query param) and logs
          # "Successfully retrieved and set token" without the token
          # itself. The engine captures npm's stderr and only dumps it on
          # failure, so green runs are unchanged.
          NPM_CONFIG_LOGLEVEL: verbose
        run: pnpm exec putitoutthere publish

      # Scaffolded workflows reference `thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v<major>`
      # (community GitHub Actions convention, e.g. actions/checkout@v4). The
      # canonical per-release tag is `putitoutthere-v<x.y.z>`; this step keeps
      # a floating `v<major>` tag pointing at the latest release in the major
      # line so the scaffold resolves. Idempotent: re-runs are a no-op when
      # the floating tag already matches the latest release. Issue #199.
      #
      # The force-fetch / latest-release lookup / idempotency / force-move
      # now live in the `advance-floating-major` engine command as tested
      # code (`src/advance-floating-major.ts`), sharing `forceMoveTag` with
      # `advance-v0` so the two floating-tag movers can't diverge.
      - name: Move floating major tag
        run: pnpm exec putitoutthere advance-floating-major

name: putitoutthere release

# Reusable workflow for publishing to crates.io, PyPI, and npm.
#
# Consumer integration (their own .github/workflows/release.yml):
#
#   on:
#     push: { branches: [main] }
#
#   jobs:
#     release:
#       uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/release.yml@v0
#       permissions:
#         contents: write
#         id-token: write
#
# That is the entire surface a consumer touches. `putitoutthere.toml`
# at the repo root is the config; nothing about that is configurable.
#
# Auth: OIDC trusted publishers on all three registries (crates.io,
# PyPI, npm) are the default and recommended path. Trusted Publishing
# binds to an *already-published* package on crates.io and npm, so the
# very first publish has no OIDC path available; callers can pass a
# long-lived `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` (crates.io) or `NPM_TOKEN` (npm)
# via `secrets:` and the OIDC exchange is skipped when present. See
# README → "Trusted publishers".
#
# This file delegates the plan + build matrix to `_matrix.yml`
# (`uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/_matrix.yml@v0`)
# so the same matrix runs on PR-time `build.yml` invocations and at
# release time. The `publish` job below is the only piece that lives
# in this file — keeping it isolated to the release path is what makes
# `build.yml` a structural-not-runtime guarantee against accidental
# publishes (publish-capable bytes simply do not exist there).
#
# The `uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0` calls inside this file
# (and inside `_matrix.yml`) resolve to the same git ref the workflow
# itself was loaded from, so the workflow + engine always agree on a
# single version.

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      environment:
        description: >-
          GitHub deployment environment to gate the publish job. Required-
          reviewers + secret scoping are configured per-environment in the
          consumer's repo settings. Default `release`.
        type: string
        default: 'release'
      node_version:
        description: >-
          Node version for plan / publish runners and for kind = "npm"
          build steps. Default `24`.
        type: string
        default: '24'
      python_version:
        description: >-
          Deprecated (#369): `kind = "pypi"` builds now fan across the
          Python versions inferred from each package's
          `requires-python` (or pinned via `python_versions` in
          `putitoutthere.toml`). This input no longer affects pypi
          builds; it is retained only so existing callers don't break.
        type: string
        default: '3.12'
      release_packages:
        description: >-
          Manual release. Comma-separated `name[@<bump|version>]`
          entries — e.g. `lib-core@minor, lib-py@1.4.0, lib-js`. Each
          entry is a package name optionally suffixed with
          `@<patch|minor|major>` or an explicit `@<X.Y.Z>` semver; a
          bare name defaults to a patch bump. When set, change
          detection is bypassed and exactly the named packages are
          released. Wire this to a `workflow_dispatch` input in your
          caller workflow to re-release packages that have no new
          commits (e.g. after a release-pipeline bug fix). Empty (the
          default) => normal change-detected release.
        type: string
        default: ''
    secrets:
      # Optional fallback for accounts where Trusted Publishing isn't
      # available, or for the very first publish of a brand-new crate
      # (Trusted Publishing on crates.io binds to an already-published
      # crate, so first-publish has no OIDC path). When set, the OIDC
      # exchange via `rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action` is skipped and
      # this token is exported to $GITHUB_ENV as CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN
      # for the engine's crates handler.
      CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN:
        required: false
      # Optional fallback for the very first publish of a brand-new npm
      # package (Trusted Publishing on npm binds to an already-published
      # package, so first-publish has no OIDC path). When set AND the
      # planned matrix contains an npm row, this token is exported to
      # $GITHUB_ENV as NODE_AUTH_TOKEN; the npm CLI then prefers the
      # long-lived token over the OIDC path. For bundled-cli / napi
      # families the same secret authenticates publishes of all per-
      # platform sub-packages on first publish; once those exist, each
      # one needs its own TP registration. Drop the secret once Trusted
      # Publishing is registered. See #302.
      NPM_TOKEN:
        required: false
    outputs:
      has_pypi:
        description: >-
          `'true'` when the planned matrix contains any pypi rows. Consumers
          gate their caller-side `pypi-publish` job on this so npm/crates-only
          repos don't need the extra job. PyPI uploads run in the caller's
          workflow context (not this reusable workflow) — see
          README → "Publishing to PyPI". Always a string ("true"/"false")
          per `workflow_call` output rules.
        value: ${{ jobs.build.outputs.has_pypi }}
      pypi_pending:
        description: >-
          `'true'` when this run handed ≥ 1 PyPI upload to the caller-side
          `pypi-publish` job and that upload has not happened yet. Publish-
          time and narrower than `has_pypi` in both directions: it is
          `'false'` on an idempotent re-run whose PyPI versions are already
          live (nothing to upload), and it is only `'true'` for packages the
          engine actually reached, so a run that died in pre-flight cannot
          trigger an upload of something it never validated (#623). Gate the
          `pypi-publish` job on this with `!cancelled()` so a failure on an
          unrelated registry no longer skips PyPI — see README →
          "Publishing to PyPI". Empty string when the publish job is
          skipped, and (per GitHub's output propagation) possibly empty when
          it failed, in which case the gate simply skips as it did before.
        value: ${{ jobs.publish.outputs.delegated }}
      released:
        description: >-
          `'true'` when this run newly published ≥ 1 package, else
          `'false'`. Unlike `has_pypi` (plan-time: "we intend to build"),
          this is publish-time: idempotent re-runs whose versions are
          already live report `'false'`. Gate a caller-side post-release
          job on it (`if: needs.release.outputs.released == 'true'`) — see
          README → "Post-release bookkeeping" (#461). Empty string when
          the publish job is skipped (empty plan); Always a string per
          `workflow_call` output rules.
        value: ${{ jobs.publish.outputs.released }}
      released_packages:
        description: >-
          JSON array of what newly shipped this run —
          `[{"name","version","tag"}, …]`, in publish (dependency) order.
          Empty array `[]` when nothing newly published. A post-release
          job reads it for a changelog section title, a docs version
          stamp, or an announcement, instead of reverse-engineering the
          set from pushed tags. See README → "Post-release bookkeeping"
          (#461). Empty string when the publish job is skipped.
        value: ${{ jobs.publish.outputs.released_packages }}

concurrency:
  group: putitoutthere-release-${{ github.repository }}
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  build:
    uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere/.github/workflows/_matrix.yml@v0
    with:
      node_version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}
      python_version: ${{ inputs.python_version }}
      release_packages: ${{ inputs.release_packages }}

  publish:
    needs: build
    if: fromJSON(needs.build.outputs.matrix || '[]')[0] != null
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    environment: ${{ inputs.environment }}
    permissions:
      contents: write
      id-token: write
    outputs:
      # #461: propagate the publish step's release facts up to the
      # reusable workflow's outputs. Same two-hop wiring `has_pypi`
      # uses (engine step → job → workflow_call.outputs). The engine
      # writes these to $GITHUB_OUTPUT only when a package newly ships.
      released: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.released }}
      released_packages: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.released_packages }}
      # #623: PyPI's upload is delegated to the caller's `pypi-publish`
      # job, so this run has NOT published those packages and has NOT
      # tagged them. The engine writes this key even when a later package
      # fails, which is what lets the caller's job gate on "PyPI's own
      # path succeeded" rather than on this job's exit code.
      delegated: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.delegated }}
    env:
      # Promote the optional caller-provided crates.io token to a job-
      # level env var so step `if:` conditions can gate on it. The
      # `secrets` context isn't available in step-level `if:` (only
      # `env`, `inputs`, `needs`, etc), so the OIDC vs caller-token
      # branching has to read through this var. Empty string when the
      # caller didn't wire the secret; non-empty when they did.
      CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN }}
      # Same shape as CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN, for npm. See #302.
      CALLER_NPM_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: ${{ inputs.node_version }}
          registry-url: 'https://registry.npmjs.org'

      # PyPI: the upload step is owned by the caller's `pypi-publish`
      # job (see README → "Publishing to PyPI"). The engine's role
      # here is plan + build artifact discovery + version-rewrite; no
      # twine, no setup-python. The git tag is owned by that job too
      # (#623) — a tag records what shipped, and until the caller
      # uploads, nothing has.

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          path: artifacts

      - name: Configure git identity for tagging
        # Annotated tags require committer identity; hosted runners have
        # none by default.
        run: |
          git config --global user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config --global user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"

      # crates.io OIDC trusted publisher exchange: ID-token -> short-
      # lived CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN. Only fires when the plan still has a
      # crates version to publish AND the caller did not supply
      # CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN via `secrets:` (issue #283). Pure JS/Python
      # repos skip the action entirely so they don't need a configured
      # trusted publisher on crates.io; callers passing a long-lived token
      # also skip it so the OIDC-minted token doesn't clobber theirs.
      #
      # #622: the gate reads `unpublished_kinds`, not the matrix. A crates
      # row is in the matrix whenever the repo has a crate — published or
      # not — so gating on the matrix ran the exchange on idempotent re-runs
      # the crates handler would skip via `isPublished`, and a failing
      # exchange (trusted publisher not registered yet, or a record that
      # hasn't propagated) killed the whole publish job before the engine
      # action ran, taking npm and PyPI with it. `unpublished_kinds` is the
      # same publish/skip determination the handler makes, hoisted ahead of
      # auth by `plan`; a kind whose registry was unreachable stays listed,
      # so a blip never silently drops a credential the publish needs.
      - name: Authenticate with crates.io (OIDC)
        if: contains(needs.build.outputs.unpublished_kinds, '"crates"') && env.CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN == ''
        id: crates-auth
        uses: rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action@v1.0.5

      - name: Export CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (OIDC)
        if: steps.crates-auth.outcome == 'success'
        env:
          CRATES_IO_TOKEN: ${{ steps.crates-auth.outputs.token }}
        run: echo "CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=$CRATES_IO_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Caller-provided token path (issue #283). Trusted Publishing on
      # crates.io binds to an already-published crate, so the first
      # publish of a brand-new crate has no OIDC path; this step lets
      # the caller supply a long-lived token via `secrets:` and have
      # the engine's crates handler pick it up through $GITHUB_ENV
      # exactly as it would the OIDC-minted one. The secret is read
      # through the job-level `CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` env var
      # because step-level `if:` cannot reference the `secrets` context.
      #
      # Deliberately still gated on the matrix, not on `unpublished_kinds`
      # (#622): this step only writes an env var, so running it with
      # nothing to publish costs nothing and cannot fail the job — the
      # narrowing above exists because a *failing OIDC exchange* took the
      # run down, and there is no exchange here to fail.
      - name: Export CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN (caller-provided)
        if: contains(needs.build.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"crates"') && env.CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN != ''
        run: echo "CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN=$CALLER_CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Caller-provided npm token path (issue #302). Mirror of the
      # CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN fallback above. Trusted Publishing on npm
      # binds to an already-published package, so the first publish of
      # a brand-new package has no OIDC path; this step lets the caller
      # supply a long-lived token via `secrets:` and have the npm CLI
      # pick it up through $GITHUB_ENV (setup-node@v6 already wires
      # NODE_AUTH_TOKEN into the .npmrc auth template). The secret is
      # read through the job-level `CALLER_NPM_TOKEN` env var because
      # step-level `if:` cannot reference the `secrets` context. When
      # NODE_AUTH_TOKEN is set, the npm CLI prefers it over the OIDC
      # path — there's no separate OIDC step to skip, just the env-var
      # presence that switches the CLI's auth mode. Drop the secret
      # once Trusted Publishing is registered against the (now-existing)
      # package; for bundled-cli / napi families each per-platform sub-
      # package needs its own TP registration.
      - name: Export NODE_AUTH_TOKEN (caller-provided)
        if: contains(needs.build.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"') && env.CALLER_NPM_TOKEN != ''
        run: echo "NODE_AUTH_TOKEN=$CALLER_NPM_TOKEN" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Build npm packages from source before `npm publish` runs.
      # The build job's `dist/` is not carried through as an artifact
      # for vanilla npm rows (artifact_path is `package.json`); the
      # publish job is a fresh checkout, so any package whose
      # package.json declares `"files": ["dist", ...]` would ship a
      # tarball missing the compiled output. Rebuild here to mirror
      # what a developer running `npm publish` locally would do.
      # napi / bundled-cli platform packages stage from artifacts/
      # via the engine's npm-platform handler and are unaffected.
      - name: Build npm packages
        if: contains(needs.build.outputs.matrix, '"kind":"npm"')
        shell: bash
        env:
          MATRIX: ${{ needs.build.outputs.matrix }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          paths=$(printf '%s' "$MATRIX" | jq -r '.[] | select(.kind == "npm") | .path' | sort -u)
          # Strict installs (`npm ci`, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile`) self-
          # heal to their non-strict form on failure. Why: bundled-cli / napi
          # consumers declare `optionalDependencies` for `<name>-<triple>@<version>`
          # platform packages that this pipeline produces. On the first publish,
          # those entries 404 on the registry; pnpm 10 silently drops 404'd
          # optionals from the lockfile when it is regenerated locally, then
          # `--frozen-lockfile` refuses on the next CI run because the lockfile
          # and package.json disagree. The `::warning::` makes the fallback
          # visible in the run log. Same shape used by `_matrix.yml`'s build
          # step. See README → Recipes → Bundled-CLI npm family.
          for path in $paths; do
            echo "::group::npm install + build at ${path}"
            pushd "${path}" > /dev/null
            if [ -f package-lock.json ]; then
              npm ci || {
                echo "::warning::package-lock.json drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to npm install"
                npm install
              }
            elif [ -f pnpm-lock.yaml ]; then
              # pnpm for the *consumer's* checkout, not ours. Deliberately a
              # literal and not ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm: that action installs
              # our build toolchain, this installs theirs, and a `uses:` step
              # cannot appear inside a run: script anyway.
              npm install -g pnpm@11
              pnpm install --frozen-lockfile || {
                echo "::warning::pnpm-lock.yaml drift (likely 404 on platform-package optionalDependencies for a brand-new bundled-cli/napi family); falling back to pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile"
                pnpm install --no-frozen-lockfile
              }
            else
              npm install
            fi
            # #287: export TARGET / BUILD so consumer build scripts that
            # dispatch on them (bundled-cli / napi) see a defined value
            # rather than `undefined`. The publish-time rebuild only runs
            # for the *main* package row (per-platform sub-packages stage
            # from artifacts/ via the engine's npm-platform handler and
            # are unaffected here), so TARGET is fixed at "main" — build
            # scripts written against the documented contract no-op on
            # TARGET=main and run vanilla TS/JS compilation otherwise.
            # BUILD is left empty because there is no single matrix-row
            # `build` mode at this point: a multi-mode package is both
            # napi and bundled-cli; the rebuild is the union view.
            TARGET=main BUILD='' npm run build --if-present
            popd > /dev/null
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

      - id: publish
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        env:
          # The repository-visibility preflight check calls the GitHub
          # API; an authenticated call gets 5000 req/hr instead of the
          # unauthenticated 60, so a busy runner never rate-limits.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        with:
          command: publish
          # publish re-runs plan internally; it must see the same
          # manual-release spec the plan job did or the two phases
          # disagree on the matrix.
          release_packages: ${{ inputs.release_packages }}

      # The engine creates annotated git tags + publishes to npm /
      # crates.io but does NOT cut GitHub Releases. Backfill that here so
      # the project's /releases page tracks the tag history. A pypi
      # package is absent from both halves at this point: its upload and
      # its tag both belong to the caller's jobs (#623), so its GitHub
      # Release is cut by the next run of this step (the tag exists by
      # then) — same idempotent backfill this step already performs.
      #
      # The no-fetch / ref-scoped-push / idempotent-create contract (#436,
      # #437) now lives in the `release-github` engine command as tested
      # code (`src/release-github/`), not inline bash — this step is pure
      # wiring. `GH_TOKEN` authenticates `gh`; the checkout's persisted
      # credentials authenticate the ref-scoped `git push`.
      - name: Create GitHub Release(s) for new tag(s)
        uses: thekevinscott/putitoutthere@v0
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
        with:
          command: release-github

name: Secret scan

# Scans the full working tree and git history for accidentally-
# committed secrets. putitoutthere handles registry tokens, so leaks
# from an npm token test fixture into a PR would be catastrophic --
# this check blocks merge.

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: secret-scan-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  gitleaks:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0 # full history

      - uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v3
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: TDD Lint

# Enforces the red/green TDD discipline from plan.md §23.7: PRs that
# modify src/ must also touch at least one *.test.ts file. CI rejects
# non-test-bearing PRs.
#
# Escape hatch: a commit in the PR range with a `Skip-Gates: <reason>`
# trailer bypasses this check. The trailer is visible in the PR commit
# list, so reviewers can push back if it's abused. See notes/gates.md.
#
# The gate logic lives in tested TypeScript (`packages/ci/src/tdd-lint/`,
# the `piot-ci tdd-lint` command), not inline bash — see AGENTS.md >
# "Repo-internal CI gates" (#452, epic #442).

on:
  pull_request:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: tdd-lint-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  require-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        # packages/ci's `prepare` script builds its dist during install, so
        # `piot-ci` is linked into node_modules/.bin and resolvable below.
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Enforce red/green TDD discipline
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
        run: pnpm exec piot-ci tdd-lint

name: Test

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]

concurrency:
  group: test-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  unit:
    name: unit (${{ matrix.os }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        os: [ubuntu-latest, macos-latest, windows-latest]
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-node

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: pnpm install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Run unit tests
        run: pnpm run test:unit

name: Testing Conventions

# Reusable, consumer-facing workflow: enforce a library's testing conventions in
# CI. Drop a single short file into your repo and opt into the full rule set with
# our defaults — no config required.
#
#   # .github/workflows/conventions.yml
#   name: Conventions
#   on: [pull_request]
#   jobs:
#     conventions:
#       uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml@v0
#
# The principle is **one suite-executing rule command → one job**, fanned out per
# language — with the four static source scans (colocated-test, its co-change variant,
# unit-lint, integration-lint) consolidated into a single `static` job per language,
# since each is a sub-second scan that would otherwise pay full job setup for <1s of
# work (#410). It runs the published `testing-conventions` binary via `npx` (a
# prebuilt, per-platform npm package — no Rust toolchain, no compile from source),
# failing the build on any violation. The shipped rule jobs are:
#
#   - static               — the four static source scans as steps of one job per
#                            language (#410): unit colocated-test (every source file has
#                            a colocated unit test, all langs; the rust arm checks inline
#                            `#[cfg(test)]` presence, #40/#274) with its co-change variant,
#                            unit lint (the unit-suite isolation lint), and integration lint
#                            (the integration mocking lints) — Python, TypeScript, Rust
#   - unit coverage        — the unit coverage floor (Python, TypeScript, and Rust
#                            via cargo-llvm-cov, #37)
#   - packaging            — no test files in the built distribution
#
# Diff-scoped variants run as their own jobs on `pull_request` only (they need
# `fetch-depth: 0` and a base ref): `unit colocated-test --base` (co-change, #161),
# `unit coverage --base` (changed-line coverage, #162), `unit mutation --base`
# (#204) — the mutation gate, binary and on by default, scoped to the changed lines
# because whole-tree mutation is too slow to gate — and `e2e verify --base` (#319),
# the freshness gate below. The `e2e verify` job (#68) checks the committed e2e
# attestation; it's verify-if-present — it runs whenever an `e2e-attestation.json`
# is committed, and `run_e2e` forces it on (#186) — and diff-scoped (#319): it
# measures freshness over the scoped source the branch changed (`<base>..HEAD`), so
# it too runs on `pull_request` only, which keeps it adoptable by a squash-merging
# repo (a squash-stale attestation never reds an unrelated PR).
#
# The `detect` job runs the repo-only detect action (`.github/actions/detect`, tested
# by pytest, #189): it scans `source` and auto-detects every supported language *present*
# (#185), and the rule jobs fan out over those. `languages` is an optional restrictor
# (empty default ⇒ auto-detect all; a JSON array ⇒ only those named), so the zero-input
# drop-in covers Python, TypeScript, and Rust alike. A language with no sources under
# `source` is dropped from the matrix and skipped, not failed (#94). The action also
# recognizes a crate (`Cargo.toml` / `*.rs`) and emits separate
# `colocated_test_languages` (#274), `integration_lint_languages`,
# `isolation_languages`, and `coverage_languages` sets that add Rust, plus
# `packaging_dist` / `e2e_attestation` flags the packaging and e2e-verify jobs gate
# on (#186). Only the co-change `*-changed` job stays on the python/typescript
# `languages` set — rust units are inline, so a sibling test can't go stale.
#
# The Packaging rule (#41) is the exception: it inspects the *built distribution*,
# not the source tree, so it doesn't ride the source matrix. It's default-on and
# build-then-scan (#186/#335): it derives the distribution build from the package's
# own manifest — `uv build` (Python `[project]`), `<pm> pack --pack-destination dist`
# (TypeScript), `cargo package` (Rust `[package]`) — provisions the toolchain, runs it
# at the derived package root, and fails if any .whl/.tar.gz (python), .tgz
# (typescript), or .crate (rust) ships a test file. So a native monorepo adopts the
# gate with `gates: ["packaging"]` and no bespoke build job. When the manifest can't
# state a build it scans a committed dist/ instead, and it's skipped — never failed —
# when no build is derivable and neither a dist/ nor an artifact exists. A prebuilt
# artifact is scanned as-is when you'd rather build it yourself:
#
#   jobs:
#     build:
#       runs-on: ubuntu-latest
#       steps:
#         - run: uv build                   # → dist/*.whl, dist/*.tar.gz
#         - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
#           with: { name: dist, path: dist/ }
#     conventions:
#       needs: build
#       uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/workflows/testing-conventions.yml@v0
#       with:
#         packaging_artifact: dist
#
# No config file is required: every check runs with sane defaults, opting a new
# library into the full set in one drop-in (#80). The coverage floor falls back to
# the language's strict default — a 100% line floor for all three (#194/#195): Python
# branch on at 100, TypeScript all four metrics at 100, and Rust `lines = 100` with
# `regions` opt-in and no branch component (#206) — when no `testing-conventions.toml`
# is present. Add a config file only to loosen a floor or declare exemptions.
#
# `languages` is a JSON array (when set) so the matrix can fan out over it directly
# (reusable-workflow inputs can't be native lists); empty — the default — means
# auto-detect every supported language present under `source` (#185).
#
# `unit coverage` (whole-tree) and `unit coverage --base` (changed-line) install, provision,
# and build at the *derived package root* (#277/#278) — the nearest directory at-or-above
# `source`, down to the checkout root, holding a `package.json` / `pyproject.toml` / `Cargo.toml`
# (`.` for a single-package repo, so an existing single-package call is unaffected). The
# TypeScript package manager, the Python environment model (a bare `uv venv`, or `uv sync` for a
# `pyproject.toml` with a `[project]` table — which also builds a maturin package's native
# module; Python is provisioned by uv either way, #399), and whether a Rust toolchain is
# auto-provisioned are all read from that root's own manifest, so a per-package-lockfile monorepo
# package (dirsql PR #410) installs and builds correctly with no configuration.
#
# `build_command` (#243/#289) and `rust_toolchain` (#263) are the remaining *escape hatches*, for a
# build the package manifest cannot express, run/provisioned at that same derived package root.
# `build_command` is a shell step run after toolchain + dependency setup and before the suite, in
# the suite-executing jobs only — `unit coverage` (whole-tree), `unit coverage --base`
# (changed-line), and `unit mutation`. It is NOT a workflow input (#289): the command lives in the
# package's own `testing-conventions.toml` as `[python] build_command` (with a required `reason`),
# discovered at the package root by `detect` exactly like `config` and surfaced as
# `needs.detect.outputs.build_command`. Set it for a Python build the auto-derivation above does not
# cover (a PEP 517 backend with no pre-build shell hook); a package with no such key leaves it empty
# ⇒ no build step. TypeScript and Rust need no key — npm's `prepare`/`postinstall` and Cargo's
# `build.rs` build their compiled modules during dependency install. The static rules
# (colocated-test, unit lint, integration lint) only parse source, and `e2e verify` checks the
# attestation rather than running the e2e suite, so none of those jobs build or import anything.
#
# `gates` (#262) is an optional allowlist naming which gates run — empty (the default) runs
# every applicable gate. The seven gate names are colocated-test, unit-lint, unit-coverage,
# mutation, integration-lint, packaging, and e2e-verify; a named gate still applies its own
# conditions (language presence, the PR event, a discoverable dist/attestation), and its
# diff-scoped variant rides with it (colocated-test covers the co-change job, unit-coverage
# the changed-line job). The allowlist is authoritative: a gate left out is skipped even when
# its forcing input (`run_e2e`, `packaging_artifact`) is set, so a scoped call stays scoped.
# Membership is the quoted-name test `contains(inputs.gates, '"<gate>"')` — the same check
# detect.py's `eligible` applies to `languages` — so a consumer that must run the
# suite-executing gates in its own build-capable jobs (a native binding whose second-language
# core these jobs cannot build, #263) still adopts the static gates here.
#
# `rust_toolchain` (#263) is the manual override that provisions a stable Rust toolchain — with
# a cargo registry + target cache — in the suite-executing jobs, before `build_command` runs.
# `unit coverage` / `unit coverage --base` already auto-provision it whenever the package root's
# manifest declares a Rust-compiling build (#277); set this by hand only for a build the
# manifest does not express, or for `unit mutation`, which does not yet derive it. The rust
# matrix arm always carries its own toolchain. `false` (the default) adds nothing beyond
# auto-derivation.
#
# Hermetic self-gating (#356): when this repo's own CI calls this workflow with no explicit
# `version`, detect derives it (from `github.repository`, which belongs to the *calling* run —
# so this can never hold for a consumer) and emits `cli_command`: the rule jobs then download
# the `hermetic-cli` artifact the repo-only caller workflow's build-cli job staged, and run the
# CLI built from HEAD instead of the published npm binary — a PR changing detect or a rule is
# gated by its own commit, not by whatever `@v0`/npm currently resolve to. There is no input
# and no job for this: the derivation lives in tested Python (internals/detect), the build in
# the caller workflows, and this file carries only guarded *steps* — a consumer's checks UI
# and execution path are byte-for-byte unchanged. See docs/internals/repo.md, "Hermetic mode".

on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      languages:
        description: 'Optional JSON array restricting which languages to check, e.g. ["python"]. Empty (the default) auto-detects every supported language present under `source` (#185).'
        type: string
        default: ''
      source:
        description: 'Directory scanned recursively for sources.'
        type: string
        default: 'src'
      version:
        description: 'testing-conventions version to run, e.g. 0.1.0 (default: latest from npm).'
        type: string
        default: ''
      config:
        description: 'Optional config file to refine the checks (coverage thresholds, exemptions). If absent, every check runs with sane defaults.'
        type: string
        default: 'testing-conventions.toml'
      base:
        description: 'Base ref for the diff-scoped `--base` jobs, diffed as `<base>...HEAD`. Used by the `*-changed` jobs, which run on `pull_request` only and check out full history.'
        type: string
        default: 'origin/main'
      run_e2e:
        description: 'Force the `e2e verify` job (#68 freshness gate) on. It is already default-on when a committed `e2e-attestation.json` is present (#186); set this to run it regardless. Needs the attestation and full git history.'
        type: boolean
        default: false
      packaging_artifact:
        description: 'Name of an uploaded build artifact (actions/upload-artifact) holding the built distributions (.whl/.tar.gz/.tgz/.crate) to check. When set, the packaging job downloads and inspects it. When empty (default), packaging still runs over a conventional dist/ found in the checkout, and is skipped only when no dist/ exists either (#186).'
        type: string
        default: ''
      gates:
        description: 'Optional JSON array naming which gates run, e.g. ["colocated-test", "unit-lint", "integration-lint"] (#262). Empty (the default) runs every applicable gate. Gate names: colocated-test, unit-lint, unit-coverage, mutation, integration-lint, packaging, e2e-verify. A named gate still applies its own conditions, and its diff-scoped variant rides with it (colocated-test covers the co-change job, unit-coverage the changed-line job). The allowlist is authoritative: a gate left out is skipped even when run_e2e / packaging_artifact is set.'
        type: string
        default: ''
      rust_toolchain:
        description: 'Manual override: provision a stable Rust toolchain (with a cargo registry + target cache) in the suite-executing jobs, before build_command runs. unit coverage / changed-line coverage already auto-provision it when the manifest at the derived package root declares a Rust-compiling build (a Cargo.toml, a maturin backend, a napi key — #277); set this by hand only for a build the manifest does not express, or for unit mutation, which does not yet derive it. The rust matrix arm always carries its own toolchain. false (the default) adds nothing beyond auto-derivation (#263).'
        type: boolean
        default: false

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  detect:
    name: Detect requested languages with sources
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      # JSON array of the requested python/typescript languages with sources under
      # `source` — the matrix the co-change `*-changed` job fans out over (rust units
      # are inline `#[cfg(test)]` modules, so a sibling test can't go stale and
      # co-change doesn't apply).
      languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.languages }}
      # The same set plus rust — the whole-tree colocated-test matrix (#274): the
      # rust arm checks inline `#[cfg(test)]` presence (#40).
      colocated_test_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.colocated_test_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.colocated_test_languages }}
      # The same set plus rust — the matrix the integration-lint job fans out over
      # (#126).
      integration_lint_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.integration_lint_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.integration_lint_languages }}
      # `unit lint` (#125): python/typescript + rust, also kept off the coverage matrix.
      isolation_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.isolation_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.isolation_languages }}
      # The `static` job's matrix (#410): the same rust-inclusive union the colocated/isolation/
      # integration sets hold, under its own name so a future per-set divergence in detect needs no
      # workflow change. The four static gates run as steps of that one job.
      static_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.static_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.static_languages }}
      # `unit coverage` (#37/#171): present python/typescript, plus rust whenever a
      # crate is present — Rust coverage is zero-config now (`lines = 100` by default,
      # #206) — the matrix the whole-tree and changed-line coverage jobs fan out over.
      # Kept as its own set so a future coverage-less language can diverge.
      coverage_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.coverage_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.coverage_languages }}
      # `unit mutation` (#204): the same set as coverage now that all three arms are at
      # parity (#201/#202/#203) — the matrix the diff-scoped mutation job fans out over.
      mutation_languages: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.mutation_languages || steps.scan_published.outputs.mutation_languages }}
      # Whether a built distribution is discoverable at the derived package_root (#280;
      # the checkout root for every single-package consumer), and whether a committed
      # e2e-attestation.json is present at the checkout root (#186) — the packaging and
      # e2e-verify jobs gate on these so they run by default and skip (never fail) when
      # absent.
      packaging_dist: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.packaging_dist || steps.scan_published.outputs.packaging_dist }}
      e2e_attestation: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.e2e_attestation || steps.scan_published.outputs.e2e_attestation }}
      # The monorepo primitive (#277): everything a suite-executing job needs to install,
      # build, and run at the right directory, derived from `source` and the package's own
      # manifest rather than a second, consumer-facing scoping input.
      package_root: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.package_root || steps.scan_published.outputs.package_root }}
      ts_package_manager: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.ts_package_manager || steps.scan_published.outputs.ts_package_manager }}
      # #475: the pnpm version handed to `pnpm/action-setup` — the consumer's own
      # `packageManager` pin echoed back when it names pnpm, since the action throws on any
      # pairing of a `version` input with a non-string-equal pin, else the `>=11` floor. Never
      # empty from a detect that has this output, so the steps below read empty as "detect
      # predates it" and fall back, the way `mutation_languages` does.
      ts_pnpm_version: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.ts_pnpm_version || steps.scan_published.outputs.ts_pnpm_version }}
      python_env: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.python_env || steps.scan_published.outputs.python_env }}
      provision_rust: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.provision_rust || steps.scan_published.outputs.provision_rust }}
      # The workspace-aware Rust build cache location (#410): the workspace root's `target/` for
      # a workspace-member crate, else the package root's own — cargo resolves the target
      # directory at the workspace root regardless of the invoking cwd, so a bare
      # `package_root`-keyed cache archives (and restores) a directory `cargo` never writes to.
      cargo_target_dir: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.cargo_target_dir || steps.scan_published.outputs.cargo_target_dir }}
      # The config file every job's `--config` should receive (#277): `inputs.config`
      # verbatim unless it's the default, in which case a package-root
      # testing-conventions.toml wins if present — so a per-package call stops naming it.
      config: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.config || steps.scan_published.outputs.config }}
      # The `build_command` declaration (#289, #335), read from the package's primary-language
      # table of that discovered config file rather than passed on the `uses:` call — the
      # suite-executing and packaging jobs run it before the suite/build. Empty when none is
      # declared (no build step).
      build_command: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.build_command || steps.scan_published.outputs.build_command }}
      # The distribution build the packaging job runs before scanning (#335) — `uv build` /
      # `<pm> pack --pack-destination dist` / `cargo package`, derived from the package-root
      # manifest — and the language whose toolchain to provision for it. Both empty when the
      # manifest structurally can't state a build, so the job falls back to a committed dist/
      # or a packaging_artifact, exactly as before.
      packaging_build: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.packaging_build || steps.scan_published.outputs.packaging_build }}
      packaging_language: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.packaging_language || steps.scan_published.outputs.packaging_language }}
      # Extra e2e freshness roots and their feature-gated excludes (#333), read from that same
      # discovered config — a shared source tree beside the package (a native core bound into
      # several bindings) that no `--scope` at-or-below the package root can reach. Rendered as
      # repeated `--extra-scope`/`--exclude` arguments the e2e-verify job appends; empty when the
      # package declares none, so a package that declares nothing is byte-identical to before.
      e2e_extra_scope: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.e2e_extra_scope || steps.scan_published.outputs.e2e_extra_scope }}
      e2e_exclude: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.e2e_exclude || steps.scan_published.outputs.e2e_exclude }}
      # The hermetic CLI invocation and the mutation job's pre-rendered adapter argument (#356),
      # decided in detect.py (tested Python — see docs/internals/repo.md, "Hermetic mode"), not here:
      # the artifact path when this repo gates itself, empty (-> the run lines' npx fallback)
      # for every other caller. Plain coalescing like every output above — no logic in YAML.
      cli_command: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.cli_command || steps.scan_published.outputs.cli_command }}
      ts_mutation_adapter_args: ${{ steps.scan_hermetic.outputs.ts_mutation_adapter_args || steps.scan_published.outputs.ts_mutation_adapter_args }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - id: scan_hermetic
        # HEAD's composite action: when the guard holds, the caller is this repo, so the
        # checkout above IS the commit under test and the local path resolves to it (#356).
        if: ${{ github.repository == 'thekevinscott/testing-conventions' && inputs.version == '' }}
        uses: ./.github/actions/detect
        with:
          languages: ${{ inputs.languages }}
          path: ${{ inputs.source }}
          config: ${{ inputs.config }}
          caller_repository: ${{ github.repository }}
          version: ${{ inputs.version }}
      - id: scan_published
        # The published action at the same @v0 the consumer pins — the path every external
        # caller takes, and this repo's own path when an explicit `version` is under test (#357).
        if: ${{ !(github.repository == 'thekevinscott/testing-conventions' && inputs.version == '') }}
        uses: thekevinscott/testing-conventions/.github/actions/detect@v0
        with:
          languages: ${{ inputs.languages }}
          path: ${{ inputs.source }}
          config: ${{ inputs.config }}
          caller_repository: ${{ github.repository }}
          version: ${{ inputs.version }}

  static:
    name: Static checks (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: detect
    # The four static gates — colocated-test (with its co-change variant), unit-lint,
    # integration-lint — run as steps of one job per language: each is a sub-second
    # source scan, so a job apiece paid ~20s of setup per gate for <1s of work. The
    # job runs when ANY member gate is allowlisted; each step guards its own gate and
    # its own language set, so `gates` semantics are unchanged (#262).
    if: ${{ (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"colocated-test"') || contains(inputs.gates, '"unit-lint"') || contains(inputs.gates, '"integration-lint"')) && (needs.detect.outputs.static_languages || needs.detect.outputs.integration_lint_languages) != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: ${{ fromJSON(needs.detect.outputs.static_languages || needs.detect.outputs.integration_lint_languages) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # Full history on pull requests only: the co-change step diffs
          # `...HEAD`; the other steps parse the tree. The values are quoted —
          # a bare 0 is falsy in expressions, so `&& 0 || 1` would always yield 1.
          fetch-depth: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && '0' || '1' }}
      - name: Download the CLI built from HEAD (hermetic, #356)
        if: needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/download-hermetic-cli
      - name: Check colocated test
        if: ${{ (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"colocated-test"')) && contains(needs.detect.outputs.colocated_test_languages || needs.detect.outputs.languages, format('"{0}"', matrix.language)) }}
        env:
          LANGUAGE: ${{ matrix.language }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} unit colocated-test --language "$LANGUAGE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH"
      - name: Check co-change vs ${{ inputs.base }}
        # `!cancelled()`: a failing earlier gate must not hide this gate's result —
        # the job still fails when any step failed. PR-only (needs the base ref);
        # rust is excluded by the rule via the `languages` membership test (inline
        # `#[cfg(test)]` units can't go stale).
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"colocated-test"')) && contains(needs.detect.outputs.languages, format('"{0}"', matrix.language)) }}
        env:
          LANGUAGE: ${{ matrix.language }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} unit colocated-test --language "$LANGUAGE" --base "$BASE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH"
      - name: Check unit lint
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"unit-lint"')) && contains(needs.detect.outputs.isolation_languages, format('"{0}"', matrix.language)) }}
        env:
          LANGUAGE: ${{ matrix.language }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} unit lint --language "$LANGUAGE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH"
      - name: Lint integration tests
        if: ${{ !cancelled() && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"integration-lint"')) && contains(needs.detect.outputs.integration_lint_languages, format('"{0}"', matrix.language)) }}
        env:
          LANGUAGE: ${{ matrix.language }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} integration lint --language "$LANGUAGE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH"

  unit-coverage:
    name: Unit-test coverage (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: detect
    # `unit coverage` enforces the Python (#26), TypeScript (#31), and Rust (#37)
    # floors. The matrix is `coverage_languages` — the requested languages with
    # sources present (#94), plus rust whenever a crate is here (Rust coverage is
    # zero-config now, `lines = 100` by default, #206) — so a requested-but-absent
    # language is skipped rather than erroring. #56 (config-driven `check`) will
    # eventually drive this from the config file. A `gates` allowlist that leaves
    # unit-coverage out skips the job (#262).
    if: ${{ (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"unit-coverage"')) && needs.detect.outputs.coverage_languages != '[]' }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        language: ${{ fromJSON(needs.detect.outputs.coverage_languages) }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
      - name: Download the CLI built from HEAD (hermetic, #356)
        if: needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/download-hermetic-cli
      # Unlike the static colocated-test / lint checks, `unit coverage` shells out
      # to the language's coverage tool — so its toolchain, and the project's own
      # test deps, must be present. Rust provisioning comes first (#278): `uv sync`
      # and an npm `prepare` script may themselves compile a Rust core, so cargo must
      # already be on PATH before the language-env steps below run.
      - if: matrix.language == 'rust'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: llvm-tools-preview
      - if: matrix.language == 'rust'
        name: Install cargo-llvm-cov
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-llvm-cov
      # Provision cargo for a build the package manifest declares — a maturin/PyO3 or
      # napi-rs build compiling a Rust core — in the python/typescript arms too (the
      # rust arm already set its own up above): auto-derived from the package root's
      # own manifest (`provision_rust`, #277), or forced by the manual `rust_toolchain`
      # override (#263) for a build no manifest field expresses. Plus a cargo registry
      # + target cache (keyed at the workspace-aware `cargo_target_dir`, #410 — the
      # workspace root's target/ for a workspace-member crate, else the package root's
      # own) so the core isn't recompiled from scratch every run.
      - if: (inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') && matrix.language != 'rust'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - if: inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true'
        name: Cache the Rust build (cargo registry + target)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git

        run: |
          set -euo pipefail

      - name: Check unit-test coverage
        env:

          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} unit coverage --language "$LANGUAGE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH"

      - if: matrix.language == 'python'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7

      - if: matrix.language == 'typescript' && (needs.detect.outputs.ts_package_manager || 'pnpm') == 'pnpm'

  mutation:
    name: Unit mutation — changed lines (${{ matrix.language }})
    needs: detect
    # `unit mutation` (#204) — the rung above coverage: a test that *runs* a changed
    # line still passes if you delete its assertions, and a surviving mutant proves it.
    # The gate is binary and on by default (no report-only mode): an un-exempted survivor
    # on a changed line fails the build, with reasoned `[[<lang>.exempt]] rules =
    # ["mutation"]` entries the only loosening. Whole-tree mutation is too slow to gate,
    # so this is **PR-only and diff-scoped** (`--base`, like coverage-changed) — only the
    # mutants on the `<base>...HEAD` changed lines are run. The matrix is
    # `mutation_languages` (the coverage set; all three arms are at parity, #201/#202/#203).
    # `mutation_languages` is a new detect output, so until a release moves `@v0` to a
    # detect that emits it (this PR's own run still pins the old `@v0`), it's empty — fall
    # back to `coverage_languages` (the identical set) so the matrix stays valid. A `gates`
    # allowlist that leaves mutation out skips the job (#262).
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"mutation"')) && (needs.detect.outputs.mutation_languages || needs.detect.outputs.coverage_languages) != '[]' }}

      fail-fast: false

        language: ${{ fromJSON(needs.detect.outputs.mutation_languages || needs.detect.outputs.coverage_languages) }}

      # BEFORE the language-env steps below — a maturin/PyO3 build triggered by `uv sync`
      # (not just an explicit `build_command`) needs cargo already on PATH. Auto-provisions
      # whenever the package root's own manifest declares a Rust-compiling build too
      # (detect's `provision_rust`, #277), not only when the caller passes `rust_toolchain`;
      # the rust arm sets its own toolchain up below, so skip it here. `target` caches at
      # the workspace-aware `cargo_target_dir` (#279, #410), mirroring the coverage jobs (#278).
      - if: (inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') && matrix.language != 'rust'

        with:

            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cargo_target_dir || format('{0}/target', needs.detect.outputs.package_root) }}

            rust-toolchain-build-${{ runner.os }}-
      # Like coverage, `unit mutation` shells out to the language's mutation engine, so
      # its toolchain — and the project's own test deps — must be present. Set up per
      # language, installed from the derived package root (#279) so a monorepo's
      # per-package lockfile/manifest is the one that's read. #56 (config-driven `check`)
      # will eventually drive this from config.
      # Provision Python with uv (#399), identically across the three suite-executing jobs so the
      # block can't drift. An installable project (a pyproject.toml with a [project] table —
      # python_env == 'uv', #277) is synced: `uv sync` installs its own dependencies AND
      # builds/installs the project itself, so a maturin package's native module compiles right
      # here (cargo already provisioned above). A plain package has no project to sync, so a bare
      # `uv venv` stands in. The union suite toolchain installs into that same venv, which goes on
      # PATH: coverage.py + pytest for the coverage gate, the testing-conventions adapter wheel for
      # mutation — `unit mutation --language python` spawns `python3 -m
      # testing_conventions.mutation.main` (#248), which the wheel puts on the path alongside its
      # cosmic-ray dependency (#258), and cosmic-ray's spawned pytest imports the project's own
      # dependencies from this same venv (#279). The wheel is named last, so the #92
      # subcommand-drift guard reads it as an install argument, not an invocation.
      - if: matrix.language == 'python'
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'
          enable-cache: true
      - if: matrix.language == 'python'
        name: Provision the Python suite environment (uv)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PYTHON_ENV: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.python_env || 'pip' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$PYTHON_ENV" = "uv" ]; then uv sync; else uv venv; fi

          echo "$PWD/.venv/bin" >> "$GITHUB_PATH"

      # project's deps (which must include @stryker-mutator/core and a runner plugin) with
      # whichever package manager the package root's own manifest/lockfile names (#279):
      # `pnpm/action-setup` only when it's pnpm, so an npm-only package doesn't require it.
      - if: matrix.language == 'typescript' && (needs.detect.outputs.ts_package_manager || 'pnpm') == 'pnpm'

        with:
          version: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.ts_pnpm_version || '>=11' }}
      - if: matrix.language == 'typescript'
        uses: actions/setup-node@v6
        with:
          node-version: 24
      - if: matrix.language == 'typescript'
        name: Install project dependencies
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          PM: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.ts_package_manager || 'pnpm' }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$PM" = "pnpm" ]; then pnpm install --frozen-lockfile; else npm ci; fi
      # Rust drives cargo-mutants over the crate. The published CLI provisions the engine
      # itself now (#242) — a pinned `cargo install` into its cache on first use — so only the
      # cargo toolchain is set up here; cache that dir so the from-source install is reused.
      - if: matrix.language == 'rust'
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - if: matrix.language == 'rust'
        name: Cache the provisioned cargo-mutants
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/testing-conventions
          key: cargo-mutants-provision-${{ runner.os }}
      # Build a caller-supplied native module before the mutation engine runs the suite
      # (#243): cosmic-ray / Stryker / cargo-mutants import the same module, so it must be
      # compiled here too; empty `build_command` ⇒ skipped. Runs at the derived package
      # root (#279) — breaking for a monorepo consumer whose command assumed the checkout
      # root (packages/rust/MIGRATIONS.md).
      - if: needs.detect.outputs.build_command != ''
        name: Run the build step (build_command)
        working-directory: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
        env:
          BUILD_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.build_command }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          eval "$BUILD_COMMAND"
      - name: Check mutation on the lines changed vs ${{ inputs.base }}
        env:
          LANGUAGE: ${{ matrix.language }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          CONFIG: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.config || inputs.config }}
          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
          # detect pre-renders the hermetic `--ts-mutation-adapter <path>` argument (#356) — the
          # npm launcher appends it on the published path, and the hermetic path bypasses the
          # launcher. Deliberately unquoted below (the $EXTRA_SCOPE pattern): empty on the
          # published path, word-split into the flag+path hermetically.
          TS_MUTATION_ADAPTER_ARGS: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.ts_mutation_adapter_args }}
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} unit mutation --language "$LANGUAGE" --base "$BASE" --config "$CONFIG" "$SCAN_PATH" $TS_MUTATION_ADAPTER_ARGS

  e2e-verify:
    name: E2E attestation freshness (e2e verify)
    needs: detect
    # Diff-scoped freshness, verify-if-present (#186, #319): on a PR, verify the
    # committed attestation covers the scoped source *this branch changed*
    # (`<base>..HEAD`) rather than the newest scoped commit in all history — the
    # same diff-relative model the changed-line coverage/mutation gates use. A
    # branch that changed the scoped source fails (with a re-attest nudge) until it
    # re-attests; a branch that changed none of it has nothing to re-attest and
    # passes. This is PR-only (it needs a base ref), so it rides the same
    # `github.event_name == 'pull_request'` gate as the other `--base` jobs — which
    # is also what makes it adoptable by a squash-merging repo: a squash rewrites
    # the attested commit into a new one on the base branch, and a history-absolute
    # walk would read that as permanently stale and red every later PR (#319). A
    # repo with no attestation is skipped, never failed; `run_e2e` forces the job
    # on. Never runs the e2e suite itself. The `gates` allowlist is authoritative
    # (#262): checked first, so a scoped call that leaves e2e-verify out skips the
    # job even when `run_e2e` is set.
    if: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"e2e-verify"')) && (inputs.run_e2e || needs.detect.outputs.e2e_attestation == 'true') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v6
        with:
          # `e2e verify --base` diffs `<base>..HEAD`, so it needs full history and
          # the base ref reachable — `fetch-depth: 0` fetches every branch, so
          # `inputs.base` (e.g. `origin/main`) resolves. Check out the PR's actual
          # head commit, not the ephemeral merge commit, which an attestation can
          # never name (it's rebuilt fresh on every push) — #293.
          fetch-depth: 0
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
      - name: Download the CLI built from HEAD (hermetic, #356)
        if: needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/download-hermetic-cli
      - name: Verify the e2e attestation is current
        env:
          VERSION: ${{ inputs.version }}
          PACKAGE_ROOT: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.package_root }}
          SCAN_PATH: ${{ inputs.source }}
          BASE: ${{ inputs.base }}
          # Extra freshness roots and their excludes (#333), pre-rendered by detect as repeated
          # `--extra-scope`/`--exclude` arguments — empty when the package declares no `[e2e]`
          # roots, so the invocation is byte-identical to before for every current consumer.
          EXTRA_SCOPE: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.e2e_extra_scope }}
          EXCLUDE: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.e2e_exclude }}
          CLI_COMMAND: ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cli_command }}
        # The attestation file lives at the derived package root (#281), matching
        # `detect`'s package-scoped `e2e_attestation` flag above; the freshness walk
        # is scoped to the caller's own `source` (#294) — narrower than the package
        # root whenever a package also carries tests/docs/config outside `source` — and
        # to the `<base>..HEAD` diff (#319), so only a change this branch made to the
        # scoped source trips it. `$EXTRA_SCOPE` / `$EXCLUDE` are detect's pre-rendered
        # `--extra-scope`/`--exclude` arguments for a shared source tree beside the
        # package (#333) — deliberately unquoted so an empty value expands to nothing
        # (byte-identical to before for a package declaring no `[e2e]` roots) and a
        # rendered value word-splits into the repeated flags. Requires a CLI new enough
        # to accept `--base` / `--extra-scope` (published by the #319 and #333 CLI PRs,
        # landed ahead of this one per AGENTS.md's "Two-step rollout for
        # workflow-consumed CLI changes").
        run: ${CLI_COMMAND:-npx -y "testing-conventions${VERSION:+@$VERSION}"} e2e verify "$PACKAGE_ROOT" --scope "$SCAN_PATH" --base "$BASE" $EXTRA_SCOPE $EXCLUDE

  packaging:
    name: Packaging (no test files in the built artifact)
    needs: detect
    # Default-on, build-then-scan (#186, #335): packaging inspects the *built distribution*,
    # not the source tree, so it doesn't ride the source matrix — but it runs by default. It
    # provisions the toolchain and builds the distribution from the manifest alone
    # (`packaging_build` — `uv build` / `<pm> pack` / `cargo package`, #335), then scans it,
    # so a native monorepo adopts the gate with `gates: ["packaging"]` and no bespoke build
    # job. It runs when an explicit `packaging_artifact` was uploaded (the prebuilt escape
    # hatch — scanned as-is, nothing built), OR detect derived a `packaging_build`, OR a
    # conventional dist/ is already committed at the derived package root (#280; the checkout
    # root for every single-package consumer). Skipped — never failed — when none holds. Each
    # distribution's language is inferred from its extension. The `gates` allowlist is
    # authoritative (#262): checked first, so a scoped call that leaves packaging out skips
    # the job even when `packaging_artifact` is set.
    if: ${{ (inputs.gates == '' || contains(inputs.gates, '"packaging"')) && (inputs.packaging_artifact != '' || needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' || needs.detect.outputs.packaging_dist == 'true') }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # A local `uses: ./...` action reference (the hermetic-cli download below) resolves from
      # the job's own checkout — every other rule job always checks out first, so it just works
      # there; this job normally skips checkout on the packaging_artifact path (nothing to
      # build), so it needs its own checkout whenever the hermetic path also needs one. This
      # must run BEFORE the artifact download below: actions/checkout always deletes the
      # workspace's existing contents before initializing its own checkout (regardless of the
      # `clean` input, which only controls git-clean *after* a checkout is already in place) —
      # checking out after the download would wipe the artifact it just fetched.
      - name: Check out the repository to build/inspect its distribution, or just to resolve the hermetic-cli download action
        if: inputs.packaging_artifact == '' || needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: actions/checkout@v6
      # Acquire the distributions one of two ways: a named upload artifact (scanned as-is),
      # or the consumer checkout above — where the build steps below produce the distribution,
      # or a committed dist/ already sits (#186).
      - name: Download the uploaded distributions
        if: inputs.packaging_artifact != ''
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact }}
          path: _packaging_artifact
      - name: Download the CLI built from HEAD (hermetic, #356)
        if: needs.detect.outputs.cli_command != ''
        uses: ./.github/actions/download-hermetic-cli
      # --- Provision the toolchain and build the distribution (#335) ---
      # Skipped entirely when a `packaging_artifact` was uploaded (it's already built) or
      # detect derived no `packaging_build` (the manifest can't state one — fall back to a
      # committed dist/). Rust provisioning comes first (#278): a `uv build` or npm `prepack`
      # may itself compile a Rust core, so cargo must be on PATH before the language env — and
      # `cargo package` needs it directly when the package itself is the crate.
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && (needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'rust' || inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') }}
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - if: ${{ inputs.packaging_artifact == '' && needs.detect.outputs.packaging_build != '' && (needs.detect.outputs.packaging_language == 'rust' || inputs.rust_toolchain || needs.detect.outputs.provision_rust == 'true') }}
        name: Cache the Rust build (cargo registry + target)
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry
            ~/.cargo/git
            ${{ needs.detect.outputs.cargo_target_dir || format('{0}/target', needs.detect.outputs.package_root) }}
          key: rust-toolchain-build-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.lock') }}

            rust-toolchain-build-${{ runner.os }}-

          set -euo pipefail

          # globstar: `**` recurses, so a nested dist is found too.

            echo "::error::no recognized built distribution (.whl / .tar.gz / .tgz / .crate) found in '$dist_root' or '$crate_root'"

          fi
          echo "checked $checked built distribution(s); no test files shipped"
